nodes.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is triangle-free if there are no $x, y \in A$ with $x + y \in A$ (the case $x = y$ is allowed).
nodes.title: Triangle-free subsets of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$

nodes.summary: There are real constants $c > 0$ and $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$, every finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and every real number $\varepsilon$ with $0 < \varepsilon \le 1$ the following holds: if every triangle-free $B \subseteq A$ misses at least $\varepsilon 2^n$ elements of $A$, then the triangle count of $A$ is at least $c \varepsilon^C 4^n$. nodes.summary: For $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the triangle count of $A$ is the number of ordered pairs $(x, y) \in A \times A$ with $x + y \in A$. Divided by $4^n$, it is the probability that $x, y, x + y \in A$ for independent uniform $x, y \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$.
